question: Is there a club or group for transfer students or commuters? I don't live on campus and kind of want to meet people
answer:
Yes. **Transfer Connection** is an Office Sponsored Organization for transfer students. It shares transfer-related updates, events and activities; visit https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/transfer-connection/ or follow @rcnjtransfers: https://www.instagram.com/rcnjtransfers/. To ask about its resources, email Meghan Gregory at mgregory@ramapo.edu. The Transfer Center & Veterans Lounge is in E211. [3][14][15]

For commuters, **Commuter Affairs** is a department committed to connecting commuter students socially and academically. Its page is https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/. [6]

Ways to meet people: connect with other commuters at Commuter Affairs events; hang out at J.Lee’s for games, programs and free popcorn; join clubs that interest you; and attend CPB/Commuter Affairs events. Commuter Affairs says it offers at least 4 events a month, with sign-ups on its Archway page during Fall and Spring semesters. [7][8][9][13] The monthly Commuter Connections newsletter also shares events and updates. [12]

For help getting involved, contact the Center for Student Involvement: csi@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7593, SC-202. [7][8][9]

question: how do i join a club here, is there a list somewhere of all the orgs
answer:
The Center for Student Involvement oversees the clubs. The college’s clubs list is at https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/; it says all clubs listed there are open to students. Clubs welcome new members, new ideas and new directions. Browse Archway (http://archway.ramapo.edu/) or download the Archway App (Apple Store: https://archway.ramapo.edu/click?linkid=08fd1643-7962-4f57-b38c-3f5860d0d5dd; Google Play: https://archway.ramapo.edu/click?linkid=919b2f1c-98bd-4bbf-866a-034302ac992d) to explore organizations. [9][13][14]
You can also stop by the Center for Student Involvement, SC 202, for information. A page recommends the Student Involvement Fair on Wednesday, August 26th to meet representatives from over 100 clubs and organizations; that date has passed. [10]
If your interests aren’t represented, inquire at the Center for Student Involvement about starting a new club or organization. Once recognized by the College, an organization is eligible for financial support from the Student Activities Allocations Committee. [12]
Contact the Center for Student Involvement: csi@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7593, SC-202. [9]

question: what cultural clubs does ramapo have

question: does ramapo have greek life? how do u rush if ur a transfer
answer:
Yes. Ramapo has Greek life; the directory gives 26 clubs under Greek Life and related categories. [1] The College describes fraternities and sororities as organized into five councils. [32]

The Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life oversees this. As a transfer, you may join in your first semester if you are in good standing with the College; no other eligibility requirements apply. [28][30] To get information, complete the [Greek Life Interest Form](https://cglink.me/2fF/s33074), which covers NPHC, PFC, IFC, CPH and UCGC. [33] The recruitment page also says to attend one in-person Hazing Prevention Workshop, sign the New Member Process Acknowledgment, and complete the required online courses assigned by the Coordinator of Fraternities, Sororities, and Student Organizations. [30] For NPC member sororities, informal recruitment occurs during fall semester and formal recruitment during spring semester. [34]

Contact the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life at ofsl@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7123; its coordinator’s office is SC-202B. [27]
